page.overview:
Who is Hua?

Hua and her younger brother Yong She and her brother were separated during their captivity, and Hua suffered repeated abuse at the hands of the corsairs, becoming especially terrified of Tagaka.

In 296 BG, the Fifth Nation organized a meeting with "Avatar" Yun on an iceberg near the South Pole, officially to sign a new treaty which would limit its raiding in return for minor concessions. When the time for the signing arrived, Hua was part of Tagaka's small entourage, carrying a bag and moving with downcast eyes. After Tagaka had raised a small ice table, Hua placed cloth on it and prepared cushions as seats. She then carefully prepared the signing itself by setting brushes, a pincher with water, and a slab inkstone in accordance to the very demanding Pianhai method. After finishing, she silently stepped back and waited nearby as Tagaka and Yun sat down, checked, and discussed the treaty.

After some discussions, Yun ultimately made the verbal demand that the Fifth Nation had to free all slaves from Zeizhou Province. He would only sign the treaty under this condition. To everyone's surprise, Tagaka casually agreed. Upon hearing this, Hua's stoic demeanor broke and she collapsed, joyfully sobbing as she realized this would mean the end of her enslavement. The Fifth Nation pirates let her weep, while Tagaka outlined that she was willing to agree to the slaves' liberation as the entire meeting was just a trap anyway. She then killed one of Yun's followers, Amak, whereupon the meeting erupted into chaos. Fifth Nation pirates emerged from the ground and dragged Yun's followers into the ice using waterbending, while the pirate queen and Yun began to duel. Meanwhile, two of Tagaka's guards grabbed Hua and dragged her away. In the anarchy, Hua eventually escaped and ran for her life, ultimately hiding for the rest of the battle in one of the iceberg's caves.

She stayed in her hideout even after the fighting had mostly ceased and she increasingly suffered from hypothermia, terrified at possibly being recaptured by the Fifth Nation pirates. After some time, however, she noticed someone moving into her cave. Believing the intruders to be pirates, she initially started to apologize for running before realizing that the newcomers were followers of Yun. Noticing that she was dangerously close to dying of the cold, the group provided Hua with blankets and provided some first aid. Weakened, she did not talk much, but smiled in gratitude at her saviors. The group informed Hua that the Fifth Nation had been defeated in the battle and Tagaka had been captured; they were part of the rescue operations that were seeking to save the pirates' captives.
